latest_nl_proof:
Let n be an integer with n > 1, and let x satisfy (n-1)/n <= x < 1. We prove the two asserted floor identities.

First, fix an integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1. Since x < 1, multiplying by the positive integer k gives kx < k. Also, from x >= (n-1)/n we get

kx >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.

Because k <= n-1 < n, we have k/n < 1, hence k - k/n >= k - 1. Therefore

k - 1 <= kx < k.

By the definition of the floor function, the unique integer in the half-open interval [k-1, k) is k-1, so floor(kx) = k - 1.

Now take k = n. From x < 1 we obtain nx < n, and from x >= (n-1)/n we obtain nx >= n-1. Hence

n - 1 <= nx < n.

Again by the definition of the floor function, floor(nx) = n - 1.

Thus for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1 we have floor(kx) = k - 1, and also floor(nx) = n - 1, exactly as claimed.
role_in_parent: Provides the explicit floor values on the candidate maximizing interval.
statement_nl: If (n-1)/n <= x < 1, then floor(k x) = k - 1 for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n - 1, and floor(n x) = n - 1.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2 (so that n-1 >= 1 and division by n is valid)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n at least 2 and every real x with (n-1)/n <= x < 1: for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1, floor of (k times x) equals k minus 1, and floor of (n times x) equals n minus 1.
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n at least 2
for all real numbers x with (n-1)/n <= x < 1
for all integers k with 1 <= k <= n-1

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter appearing in bounds for x and k

variables.name: k
variables.role: quantified variable indexing the first floor identity

witness_dependencies: The value k is independent of x beyond the fact that the conclusion uses the same n and x; k only ranges over integers with 1 <= k <= n-1.
The second conclusion floor(n x) = n - 1 depends only on the same n and x; it is not an additional existential choice.
